trigger_condition: _validate_chargeback_attribution only inspects the incoming chargeback_attribution request parameter; when a caller clears the cost center (clear_cost_center=True) without also resetting chargeback_attribution, resolved_cost_center_id becomes None but a project whose chargeback_attribution was already 'cost_center' keeps that value unchanged, leaving cost_center-attributed billing with no linked cost center
guard_snippet: no check re-validates the effective post-update attribution (project.chargeback_attribution when chargeback_attribution param is None) against the newly resolved cost_center_id of None
potential_consequence: a project can end up persisted with chargeback_attribution='cost_center' and cost_center_id=None after a plain cost-center-clearing update, an inconsistent state the CHECK constraint does not catch (it only restricts the two string values, not the cross-field relationship), and no test exercises this because the existing clear_cost_center test builds a fresh Application whose chargeback_attribution defaults to 'project'
evidence: Read _validate_chargeback_attribution at src/codemie/service/project/project_service.py:298-311: it returns immediately unless the chargeback_attribution argument itself equals 'cost_center', never consulting the project's existing attribution. Read application_repository.update_project at src/codemie/repository/application_repository.py:704-718: application.cost_center_id is always overwritten with the resolved value while application.chargeback_attribution is only overwritten when the parameter is not None. Read test_clear_cost_center_passes_none (tests/codemie/service/project/test_project_service_delete_update.py:628-652): it uses _make_app() which constructs a bare Application relying on the model default chargeback_attribution='project', so the scenario of a pre-existing 'cost_center' attribution combined with clear_cost_center is never constructed or asserted. Grepped the whole project/service test directory for 'clear_cost_center' and found only this one test.

trigger_condition: chargeback_attribution is typed as an unconstrained Optional[str] at the API layer, and the service-level validator only branches on the value 'cost_center'; any other non-null string (e.g. a typo or unsupported value) skips all Python-level validation and is forwarded straight to application_repository.update_project, which unconditionally assigns it to the ORM object and only fails on session.flush() via the new ck_applications_chargeback_attribution CHECK constraint
guard_snippet: no application-level rejection such as raising a 400 ExtendedHTTPException when chargeback_attribution not in (None, 'project', 'cost_center')
potential_consequence: a malformed chargeback_attribution value produces an unhandled sqlalchemy IntegrityError instead of a clean validation error, and no test in the router or service suites ever sends a value other than 'project' or 'cost_center' so this path is never exercised
evidence: Read ProjectUpdateRequest at src/codemie/rest_api/routers/projects.py:263-283: chargeback_attribution has no Literal/enum constraint.
